full_judgment:
This rule was obtained by the defendant-petitioners challenging the judgment and decree dated 30.5.83 passed by Mr. Md. Badruzzaman, District Judge, Chittagong in Other Appeal No. 61 of 1983 reversing the judgment and decree dated 29.12.82 passed by Mr. Md. Taha Mollab, Munsif, 1st Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 393 of 1980. 

 5. The learned District Judge considered Ext..1., which is reply by the plaintiff during the departmental proceeding, an officer other than the enquiry officer did issue question and there is no authentication by the enquiry officer concerned and .1 (1) i.e. the question and answer by said Afsaruddin Ahmed, Accountant who was the passing officer-in-charge of the defective notes section and Mr. Manir Ahmed in-charge of the defective notes counter and their statement were recorded by an offices other than the enquiry officer. There is nothing in the enquiry report that the plaintiff was given any chance to cross-examine the said witnesses of the defendants nor the plaintiff was given any chance to adduce his own witness in support of his case. The learned District Judge in his judgment has quoted rules II of the Book-let of Instructions and came to a finding that in the present case, the prosecution witnesses were neither examined in presence of the plaintiff nor the latter was given any opportunity at any stage of the proceeding to cross-examine them to prove his innocence. The plaintiff was not given any opportunity to offer an evil explanation about the evidence led against him by the said prosecution witnesses. Therefore the learned District Judge came to the conclusion that the proceeding leading to the dismissal of the plaintiff violated the Rules 4 to 17 of the Booklet of Instruction and it also violated the principles of natural justice. After recording the findings the learned District Judge allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and decreed the suit declaring the dismissal of the plaintiff from service as illegal and consequently the order rejecting the plaintiffs appeal by the Governor is also illegal. Being dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court the defendant-petitioners obtained this Rule.
